How it works

If you have an old non-running vehicle that you want to send to scrap, and at the same time, get cash for it, our company is glad to help you. There are three simple steps you need to complete:

  • Call Us

    You can contact us online or call our customer service department and tell us “I want to sell my junk car.” Our representative will ask basic questions about your junk car's year, make, model, mileage, and condition.

  • Get an Offer

    We will assess your vehicle and make an offer. We take care of all the paperwork. You can get the money in cash when picking up your car or check. You can be sure you will not face any hidden additional costs.

  • We Come to You

    After you have accepted the offer, our representatives will agree with you on when we can pick up your car. We would like to draw your attention to the fact that we can tow the vehicle on the day of the deal or at any other agreed-upon time.

Junk Car Buyer Vs. Junkyard Vs. Auto Recycler Vs. Auto Wrecker

How to Sell a Car to a Junkyard?

Selling a car to salvage yards in Baltimore, Maryland can be a straightforward procedure provided you partner with a trusted junker. In most cases, all you need to get started is to send a request via the website of a scrap yard in Baltimore, Maryland and wait for a call. Afterward, you schedule a quick appointment with a local buyer representative, get and sign an offer, and arrange a pickup time. Provided that all the documentation is handled by a junker, getting rid of your used car is as simple as making a few calls and appointments.

How Can I Get The Best Deal For My Junk Car?

When you sell a junk car for salvage yards in Baltimore, MD, be aware of several key factors that impact the end cost offered. Among them are the following:

Condition of the Car.

The state of the used car is a crucial price-formation factor. Wrecked, flooded, and just cars in poor conditions are cheaper than ones that still can run. That’s why you should always do timely technical maintenance or at least check your vehicle before contacting auto wreckers.

Selling a car with a clean title in Alabama is the easiest way to sell your vehicle

A clean title should be in your name, free of any liens, and without salvage, rebuilt, junk, or other title brands. Simply sign the title, provide a valid photo ID, and complete the required paperwork. In many cases, the entire sale can be completed in a single visit.

We buy
We buy vehicles in any condition, including those with a clean title. Clean-title vehicles typically qualify for the highest cash offers.
Eligibility Requirements

To sell a salvage-title vehicle in Alabama, you generally need:

  • An Alabama Certificate of Title issued in your name.
  • A title that is free of active liens, or a lien release if the loan has already been paid off
  • A valid government-issued photo ID, with the name matching the title.
  • No unresolved ownership issues or outstanding lender claims.
  • An odometer disclosure completed when required under Alabama title regulations.
How the Process Works
  1. An Alabama Request a free vehicle appraisal by providing your VIN, vehicle condition, and basic information. of Title issued in your name.
  2. Receive a cash offer based on your vehicle's condition, market value, and clean title status.
  3. Sign the title and any required transfer documents, including the Assignment of Title and odometer disclosure, if applicable.
  4. Our representative arrives, verifies the VIN and paperwork, and completes the transaction.
  5. You get paid on the spot, and we handle the vehicle pickup. In most cases, you do not need to visit the Alabama Department of Revenue yourself.
How a Clean Title Affects Your Offer
A clean title usually qualifies your vehicle for the highest possible offer because it has no title-branding issues. The final amount still depends on the vehicle's condition, mileage, demand, and current market value.

How to Sell a Car with a Salvage Title in Alabama

Get a Cash Offer for Your Salvage Title Car in {City}, Alabama

Complete our quick online form or give us a call to receive a free, no-obligation quote.
Instant offer

Selling a car with a clean title in Alabama is the easiest way to sell your vehicle

In Alabama, a salvage title is generally issued when an insurance company declares a vehicle a total loss, typically because the cost of repairs equals or exceeds 75% of the vehicle's fair retail value under Alabama law. A vehicle with a salvage title can still be sold without being rebuilt. Many buyers purchase salvage vehicles for parts, recycling, export, or rebuilding by a licensed rebuilder.

We buy
We buy vehicles with salvage titles. While offers are usually lower than for clean-title vehicles, you'll still receive a fair cash offer based on your vehicle's condition and value.
Eligibility Requirements

To sell a salvage-title vehicle in Alabama, you generally need:

  • An Alabama Salvage Certificate of Title issued by the Alabama Department of Revenue (ALDOR).
  • The salvage title in your name, showing you as the legal owner.
  • A valid government-issued photo ID that matches the name on the title.
  • Written disclosure that the vehicle has a salvage title, as required by Alabama law.
  • If the vehicle is designated as "Vehicle Sold for Parts Only – Nonrebuildable," it cannot be legally rebuilt for road use.
How the Process Works
  1. Submit your VIN along with photos showing the vehicle's condition and damage.
  2. We evaluate the vehicle based on its salvage status, condition, and current market value.
  3. We prepare any required salvage-title disclosure paperwork.
  4. Sign the Salvage Certificate of Title and complete any required transfer documents, including the odometer disclosure if applicable.
  5. Get paid on the spot, and we'll pick up the vehicle from {City}.
How a Clean Title Affects Your Offer
Vehicles with a salvage title typically receive offers that are 30% to 50% lower than comparable clean-title vehicles, depending on the extent of the damage, repairability, demand for parts, and current market conditions. A salvage title does not automatically mean the vehicle is only suitable for parts. Many salvage vehicles are later rebuilt and returned to the road after meeting Alabama's inspection requirements.

How to Sell a Car with a Non-Repairable or Junk Title in Alabama

Sell Your Non-Repairable or Junk Title Car in {city} — Free Towing Included

Instant offer

Non-Rebuildable Vehicles: Alabama Junk Certificate

If your vehicle has sustained such extensive damage that repairing it is no longer economically practical and it no longer qualifies for a salvage title, Alabama issues a Junk Certificate (Parts-Only Certificate).

This is the vehicle's final legal status. Once a Junk Certificate has been issued, the vehicle cannot receive another title or be registered again. It may only be dismantled for parts or recycled by a licensed automotive recycler or salvage facility.

We buy
We buy vehicles with a Junk Certificate strictly for parts recycling or scrap. These vehicles cannot be returned to the road.
Eligibility Requirements
  • You have an Alabama Junk Certificate or an out-of-state title or bill of sale identifying the vehicle as junk, parts-only, nonrepairable, or certificate of destruction.
  • Under Alabama law, these vehicles can only be sold to a licensed automotive recycler, salvage dealer, dismantler, or other authorized buyer, depending on the vehicle's legal status. They cannot legally be sold to a private buyer for road use.
  • Once a Junk Certificate has been issued in Alabama, the vehicle is permanently classified as non-repairable. This status is reported through the National Motor Vehicle Title Information System (NMVTIS) and cannot be reversed.
Step-by-Step Process
  1. Send us your VIN and a few photos so we can verify the vehicle's junk or non-repairable status.
  2. We calculate your offer based on the vehicle's scrap value and any reusable parts.
  3. Provide your Junk Certificate, title, or bill of sale, along with a valid government-issued ID.
  4. We schedule free vehicle pickup anywhere in {city}, in most cases at no additional cost.
  5. Get paid on the spot by cash or another available payment method.
How a Junk Title Affects Your Offer
Vehicles with a Junk Certificate receive the lowest valuation because they cannot legally be rebuilt or registered again. The offer is generally based on scrap metal value plus the value of reusable components, such as the engine, transmission, catalytic converter, wheels, or electronic modules.

How to Sell a Car Without a Title (Lost or No Title) in Alabama

No Title? Find Out How to Sell Your Car in {city}, Alabama

Instant offer

Lost or Missing Title? You Can Still Sell to Us

In Alabama, a salvage title is generally issued when an insurance company declares a vehicle a total loss, typically because the cost of repairs equals or exceeds 75% of the vehicle's fair retail value under Alabama law. A vehicle with a salvage title can still be sold without being rebuilt. Many buyers purchase salvage vehicles for parts, recycling, export, or rebuilding by a licensed rebuilder.

We buy
We buy vehicles without a title. You'll need alternative proof of ownership before the sale can be completed.
Eligibility Requirements
  • You have at least one document that helps establish ownership, such as a vehicle registration in your name, a bill of sale, insurance records, or other supporting documentation.
  • If a bonded title is required, it must be obtained through the Alabama Department of Revenue (ALDOR) Motor Vehicle Division using Form MVT 10-1A. The required surety bond amount depends on the vehicle's value.
  • A bonded title remains in effect for three years, during which ownership can be legally transferred.
  • A bonded title generally is not available for vehicles acquired solely for parts, dismantling, or without sufficient proof of ownership.
Step-by-Step Process
  1. We review the ownership documents you have available, such as your registration, bill of sale, or other records.
  2. If a bonded title is required, we'll explain how to complete Form MVT 10-1A and what documents you'll need to submit to ALDOR.
  3. We can provide a preliminary vehicle valuation while your ownership documentation is being completed.
  4. Once your bonded title or replacement title has been issued, we complete the sale just as we would with a standard vehicle title.
  5. Get paid on the spot, and we'll pick up the vehicle from {City}.
How Missing a Title Affects Your Offer
Simply not having the title usually does not reduce your vehicle's value. In most cases, it only affects how quickly the sale can be completed because ownership must be verified before payment and transfer can legally take place.
